title: Button "Setup a NAP network" in bluetooth connection settings does nothing.
line: The Bluetooth device page now shows "Setup NAP Network…" when the phone has no network connection yet, and clicking it creates one.
explanation: The KCM asks plasma-nm whether a Bluetooth network connection already exists for the device and used the answer as "show the button". So the Setup NAP/DUN buttons appeared only when a connection was already there, and plasma-nm's addBluetoothConnection then returns early because it exists: the click silently does nothing, while devices without a connection never got the button. The change inverts the check so the buttons show only when no connection exists yet and the device is connected.

commits.message:
kcm: Show network setup buttons only when there's no connection yet

The "Setup NAP Network…" and "Setup DUN Network…" buttons appeared
only when the device already had a network connection, where clicking
does nothing. Show them when no connection exists, so they can set it up.

BUG: 441665

patches.diff:
From 551c5a9eb9cd2821ebe0517feeca90dab91bd9ea Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:18:48 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] kcm: Show network setup buttons only when there's no
 connection yet
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

The "Setup NAP Network…" and "Setup DUN Network…" buttons appeared
only when the device already had a network connection, where clicking
does nothing. Show them when no connection exists, so they can set it up.

BUG: 441665
---
 src/kcm/ui/Device.qml | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/src/kcm/ui/Device.qml b/src/kcm/ui/Device.qml
index 85814855..6a1d59e5 100644
--- a/src/kcm/ui/Device.qml
+++ b/src/kcm/ui/Device.qml
@@ -55,10 +55,10 @@ KCMUtils.SimpleKCM {
         function onNetworkAvailable(service: string, available: bool): void {
             switch (service) {
             case "dun":
-                dunButton.visible = available && root.device.connected;
+                dunButton.visible = !available && root.device.connected;
                 break;
             case "nap":
-                napButton.visible = available && root.device.connected;
+                napButton.visible = !available && root.device.connected;
                 break;
             default:
                 break;
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master, phone offering NAP with no network connection yet: no Setup NAP Network button.
Master, once a NAP connection exists the button appears; clicking it does nothing (no new connection, no dialog).
With the fix, no connection yet: the Setup NAP Network button is shown; clicking it creates the connection in NetworkManager.
With the fix, after the connection exists: the button is gone.

review.text: Good root-cause diagnosis: the KCM was indeed showing the Setup NAP/DUN buttons only when a connection already existed, making clicks a silent no-op. However, simply negating `available` inside `onNetworkAvailable` in Device.qml leaves the signal semantics contradicting its name, and clicking the button still leaves it visible with no feedback until the user reopens the page, so it still appears to do nothing from the user's perspective.
changes: Fix the inverted boolean semantics cleanly instead of writing `visible = !available` in `onNetworkAvailable`: either invert the boolean in `Bluetooth::checkNetworkInternal` (C++) so `networkAvailable` accurately means network setup is available, or rename the signal and parameter (e.g. `networkConnectionExists(service, exists)`).

Refresh the network availability state after `setupNetworkConnection` completes (e.g. re-run `checkNetworkInternal` when the D-Bus call finishes) so the Setup NAP/DUN button hides immediately once the connection is created instead of staying visible until the page is reopened.

reviews.text: The root cause is right. The pre-2020 widget KCM (bc0a93df) showed the NAP/DUN buttons only when !exists, and the QML rewrite (282a98f9) dropped the negation, so the button only showed in the state where plasma-nm's addBluetoothConnection returns early. Inverting the check restores the intended behaviour, and the evidence shows the button now appears with no connection and a click creates one through plasma-nm. That closes the title. The reporter's real goal of sharing the PC's internet to the phone is a different feature that this button never offered. Nit: the button stays visible after a click until the page is reopened (re-running checkNetworkConnection() after setup would hide it), and the signal argument 'available' now reads backwards. Neither blocks the MR.
